articleTitle: Vision Transformers (ViT) for Enhanced Skin Cancer Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The deployment of artificial intelligence for the analysis of dermoscopic images has catalyzed significant advancements in the early detection and subsequent treatment of skin cancer, which continues to escalate in prevalence globally, presenting a formidable public health challenge. Notable progress has been achieved in the realm of skin cancer detection through the adoption of convolutional neural networks (CNNs), which constitute the core architecture for deep learning in this field. However, while this approach excels at extracting features from minor elements within the images, it falls short in accurately identifying and localizing critical regions. As a result, our research has led us to utilize Vision Transformer (VIT) models to enhance skin cancer detection and classification. By applying these VIT models to various datasets and comparing the results with those obtained from CNNs and other models, we have achieved remarkable outcomes. Specifically, we attained an accuracy exceeding 96% with the VIT-B16 model on the benign versus malignant skin cancer dataset and 94% on the HAM10000 dataset. These findings underscore the potential of Vision Transformer models in improving diagnostic accuracy and advancing the field of dermatological AI.

articleTitle: AI Innovations in Photovoltaic Power Prediction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Accurate prediction of solar energy production is essential for integrating photovoltaic (PV) systems into the global energy grid, ensuring grid stability, and optimizing energy management. Traditional PV forecasting methods often face challenges in accounting for the inherent variability in solar radiation and atmospheric conditions. This paper proposes an innovative approach using machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) techniques, particularly Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, to improve short-term PV energy forecasts. Unlike previous models, our work introduces a new combination of input variables, including real-time meteorological data and optimized preprocessing techniques, leading to improved prediction accuracy under varying environmental conditions. The study also demonstrates the importance of high-quality data acquisition, advanced feature selection, and rigorous model training processes for achieving reliable forecasting results. By evaluating multiple models across different scenarios, this research contributes a novel methodology for enhancing the precision of PV power prediction, making it highly suitable for real-world applications in renewable energy integration.

articleTitle: A Probabilistic Data-Driven Framework for Wind Power Curtailment Assessment
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The increasing presence of dispersed inverter-based resources, the complex market-driven power transactions and the growing number of non-linear electrical loads make modern power systems more susceptible to dynamic disturbances. In this context, it is essential to improve the resilience of power systems against these disturbances by integrating the Dynamic Security Assessment (DSA) tools with knowledge discovery modules aimed at promptly inferring actionable information from massive and heterogeneous data, identifying corrective actions to mitigate the dynamic effects of significant perturbation events. In this context, curtailing renewable power generators is a crucial measure that the DSA should implement to maintain power system stability following severe grid disturbances. For this purpose, this paper proposes a data-driven probabilistic method to infer the hidden mappings between aggregated electricity market data and the corresponding wind power curtailment computed by an actual DSA module. The paper presents and discusses experimental results obtained by applying the proposed method in predicting the behavior of a real DSA tool, analyzing the Italian electricity market data, and highlighting the most promising future research directions in this field.

articleTitle: Dynamic Switching Enhancement for Electric Vehicle Charging Station Real-Time Operation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Electric Vehicle (EV) Charging Station (CS) may have various Charging Columns (CC) with one or two Charging Points (CP). When two CPs are used, the power rate of the charging column is constant, but each CP can vary its power rate. The scheduling of the CP is commonly not controlled, and one CP could provide the maximum rate of the CC, limiting the availability of the other CP. This operation could reduce the infrastructure utilization rate while worsening the user charging experience. Therefore, the scope of this paper is to propose a dynamic switching to vary the power rate of the CPs taking into account the EV's charging demand. This would mitigate the lack of flexibility regarding the CP availability at every instant. The results show that this approach reduces the charging times, increases the EV satisfaction rate, and improves charging point operator profitability.

articleTitle: Convolutional Neural Networks for Accurate MRI-Based Brain Tumor Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Brain tumor classification stands as a pivotal aspect of neuro-oncology, critical for precise diagnosis and tailored treatment strategies. This study presents an innovative approach harnessing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to revolutionize automated brain tumor classification utilizing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data. Through meticulous training and validation, our CNN model showcases exceptional efficiency in discerning subtle patterns within MRI images, facilitating precise classification across diverse tumor types. Comparative analysis validates the superiority and clinical significance of our approach over established methodologies. Moreover, our research achieves outstanding accuracy, with our CNN model attaining a remarkable 99.88% accuracy rate and boasting a remarkably low loss of 0.29%.

articleTitle: Bond Graph Analysis and Regulation of Battery Cycles: Real Time Current and Voltage
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This article describes the analysis and regulation of battery cycles, focusing on the real-time management of current and voltage using PWM charge controllers. We employ the bond graph approach to model the dynamic interactions within battery systems. A detailed model of a lead-acid battery powered by a Photovoltaic source has been developed, capturing its main electrical characteristics. The PWM charge controller dynamically adjusts the current and voltage in real-time to ensure optimal efficiency and extend battery life. Our results show that the bond graph model combined with real-time control significantly improves battery cycle regulation. The method was validated through simulations and real-time experiments, confirming its effectiveness for battery management systems.

articleTitle: Enhanced Genetic Algorithms Based Optimization of ARX-Laguerre Model Parameters: Application to 2-Dof Helicopter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper explores the application of genetic algorithms to optimize ARX-Laguerre model parameters. It outlines the ARX-Laguerre modeling process and genetic algorithm principles. A fitness function is chosen and the impact of noise on it is addressed. A new methodology for optimizing Laguerre poles using genetic algorithms is proposed. It is used in modeling a real 2-Degree-of-Freedom helicopter offering valuable insights for real-world applications.

articleTitle: Using Support Vector Regressor and Random Forest Regressor to Predict Absorption Coefficient of CdSe/ZnTe Used for Photovoltaic Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper demonstrates two Machine Learning (ML) algorithms approaches to predict and analyze the absorption coefficient of CdSe/ZnTe used for solar photvoltaique cells. Random Forest Regressor (RFR) and Support Vector Regressor (SVR) are used as ML algorithms at different Radius from 1.6 to 2.1 nm. By a comparison with theoretical data, the simulation results show a number of interesting properties for the prediction of the absorption coefficient at different Radius. In which the most successful model found is the RFR model. The coefficient of determination <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}})$</tex> ranges impressively from 0.997 to 0.999, demonstrating the model's exceptional ability to explain data patterns and account for variability. The results are highly promising, with an exceptionally low Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{3.6}\times \mathbf{10}^{-\mathbf{3}}$</tex>, indicating minimal deviations between the predicted values and the actual data points at a radius of 1.6 nm. Moreover, the lowest Mean Square Error (MSE) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{2.9}\times \mathbf{10}^{-\mathbf{4}}$</tex> at a radius of 1.6 nm highlights the minimal average difference between predicted and actual values, emphasizing the model's precision. The Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{1.7}\times \mathbf{10}^{-\mathbf{2}}$</tex> further reinforces the model's consistency and accuracy in making predictions across the dataset. The input of the model of vector includes 1500 data points representing Photon energy values. However, the output layer gives three vectors of 1500 data points representing absorption coefficient for different Radius (R= 1.6 nm; R= 1.9 nm; R= 2.1 nm). According to others models, the RFR approach offers highly precise and swift predictions using only a small set of theoretical data. As a result, it speeds up the process of characterizing new absorption coefficient of CdSe/ZnTe.

articleTitle: High-sensitive SPR device based on MgF2 prism, Ag, and graphene for detection heavy metal ions in water
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: An optical sensor incorporates an MgF2 prism, silver (Ag), and graphene is investigated for sensing applications. Significant results for sensitivity and reflection at resonance are achieved after optimizing the thickness layers of silver and graphene. An exact method based on electromagnetic theory is used to examine the sensor's reflectance in wavelength interrogation. Our optimized biosensor provides an ultra-high sensitivity varied from 20800 to 41600 nm/RIU and a reflection depth interposed between 1.94% and 2.38%, for a refractive index belonging to the interval [1.33, 1.34]. Using our biosensor, we successfully detected heavy metal ions <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Hg}2+, \text{Pb}_{9}^{2+}\text{Cu}^{2+}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{Zn}^{2+}$</tex> in water, with maximum sensitivity of 37555, 36111, 32933, and 34666 nm/RIU, respectively.

articleTitle: HexTileConnect: Achieving Connected k-Coverage in Planar Wireless Sensor Networks Using Irregular Hexagonal Tessellation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In wireless sensor networks (WSNs), achieving network connectivity and sensing coverage (or simply coverage) simultaneously is crucial for ensuring the desired quality of service of the underlying sensing application. The two main functions of sensors in WSNs are sensing and communication, which are assessed using the coverage and connectivity metrics. This study focuses on the problem of connected <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{k}$</tex> -coverage in planar WSNs (PWSNs), denoted by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\boldsymbol{CC}_{\boldsymbol{k}}\boldsymbol{P})$</tex>, where every point in a planar field of interest (PFoI) is covered by at least <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{k}$</tex> sensors at the same time, with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{k} \geq\boldsymbol{1}$</tex>, and all the participating sensors are mutually connected. To address this problem, our study follows a series of steps: First, we investigate the sensor placement problem, and compute the required sensor density for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{k}$</tex> -coverage of a PFoI. Second, we consider tiling a field using planar convex polygonal tiles with no gaps or overlaps, ensuring effective coverage. Third, we identify the necessary relationship between the sensors' communication and sensing ranges to ensure network connectivity. Fourth, we propose an energy-efficient <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{k}$</tex> - coverage protocol using the “best” planar convex polygonal tile. Our goal is to extend the network lifespan while achieving <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{k}$</tex> - coverage of a PFoI with a minimum number of sensors. We support our analysis with simulation results.

articleTitle: GaN Switch-Based Rectifier for Wave Energy Conversion with Supercapacitor Storage System
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The output power of the wave energy conversion has variable frequency and voltage, which must be regulated to supply to the grid or the storage system. Many rectifier topologies with different control techniques have been proposed based on the mechanical wave energy conversion (WEC) system. These techniques primarily rely on the voltage profile and frequency variations without profoundly considering the conversion efficiency of the electrical components. We propose a gallium nitride (GaN) switch-based rectifier for a WEC with the power storage system in the supercapacitor. This study analyzes the smoothing of voltage and electrical power conversion efficiency of the rectifier. To assess the efficiency of the power conversion stage, we replaced the traditional insulated-gate bipolar transistor (IGBT) and high electron mobility transistor (HEMT) switches with GaN-HEMT in the rectifier circuit. The scalar pulse width modulation technique has been analyzed for voltage smoothing and fixed frequency of the WEC. Mathematical analysis for power loss and passive filter design is carried out and compared with the Si-IGBT three-phase rectifier. Simulation results are discussed using MATLAB/Simulink based on real-time data for the supercapacitor charging power, switching losses, and total harmonic distortion.

articleTitle: Response Surface Methodology and Artificial Neural Network for Optimization of Dopamine Sensor Based on Nanocomposites Modified Glassy Carbon Electrode
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive investigation into the optimization of the electrochemical response of a sensor using the Box-Behnken Design (BBD) response surface methodology (RSM). The preparation of a modified Ag@MIL-101/GCE electrode is described in detail, followed by an overview of the apparatus and electrochemical testing procedure. To identify the key factors influencing the electrical response of the sensor, we present the design of response surface experiments followed by ANDV A analysis. The use of artificial neural networks (ANN s) to model nonlinear relationships and accurately predictsensor responses is also discussed. The ANN modeldemonstrated exceptional performance, with correlation coefficients of 0.96175 for training, 0.99598 for validation, and 0.99998 for testing, leading to an overall correlation coefficient of 0.97765. The model also achieved a low root mean square error (RMSE) of 0.44 and a mean error close to zero (−0.013704), reflecting its accuracy and robustness. Confirmation experiments validated the proposed model, with the experimental peak current of 13.25 μA closely matching the predicted value of 13.18 μA. These results highlight the practical utility of the model in optimizing electrochemical sensor design for dopamine detection.

articleTitle: Study and Simulation of Green Hydrogen Production Systems Coupled With Concentrated Photovoltaic Generators
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: As part of its economic recovery plan, Tunisia places a strong emphasis on producing and utilising low-carbon and green hydrogen due to its abundance of energy resources, especially its solar potential, and its commitment to achieving energy transition goals. Conventional hydrogen extraction methods rely on heat or electrical energy. Concentrating photovoltaic (CPV) modules can be used to produce hydrogen using a water electrolyser with solar electricity, thus eliminating the need for fossil fuels and carbon dioxide emissions. In this article, an assessment of the technical potential for producing hydrogen from this system is studied. The paper's main focus is on the integration of electrolysis hydrogen production with renewable energy like concentrated PV (CPV). In the Matlab/Simulink environment, a complete modelling of the CPV electrolysis system is developed. Simulation results indicate that employing a DC/DC buck converter with MPPT control enables a more effective alignment between the CPV generator and alkaline electrolysis.

articleTitle: Real-Time Face Detection and Recognition by the NAO Robot Using YOLO5 Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper presents a face detection and recognition system implemented on the NAO robot using the YOLO5 algorithm. The system is capable of identifying both known and unknown individuals in real-time. By integrating the YOLO5 algorithm with NAO's facial recognition capabilities, the system can accurately detect and recognize faces. The YOLO5 algorithm enables real-time object detection by processing images in a single pass through a deep convolutional neural network. By leveraging YOLO's efficiency and accuracy, combined with NAO's facial recognition capabilities, the system achieves reliable face detection and recognition. Extensive testing was conducted to evaluate the system's performance. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed system in detecting and recognizing faces in various environments and lighting conditions.

articleTitle: Evaluation of ANN, PSO-ANN, TLBO-ANN, and SVR Models for Fe(III) Ion Biosorption
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This study uses a Box-Behnken design (BBD) to optimize the process parameters for Fe(III) removal. A total of 45 randomized experiments were conducted. Various models, including Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Particle Swarm Optimization-ANN (PSO-ANN), Teacher Learning Based Optimization-ANN (TLBO-ANN), and Support Vector Regression (SVR), were developed and compared. The ANN model showed good performance with RMSE of 0.532102, MAPE of 0.204321, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> of 0.879105, but needed further optimization. The PSO-ANN model showed exceptional accuracy with an RMSE of 0.027668, MAPE of 0.006530 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> of 0.999673. The TLBO-ANN model also showed high accuracy with an RMSE of 0.027906, MAPE of 0.009095, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> of 0.999667. The SVR model performed well with an RMSE of 0.100851, MAPE of 0.100859 and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> of 0.995657. Comparative analysis showed that the PSO-ANN model achieved the highest accuracy and the lowest prediction error, making it the most reliable model for high accuracy applications.

articleTitle: Solar Cells Fabricated by Spray Pyrolysis Based on CU2NiSnS4 Chalcogenide
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Chalcogenide layers of CU<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>NiSnS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (CNTS) were controllably synthesized by a facile spray pyrolysis technique. The thickness effect variation on the structural, chemical, optical and electrical properties of the CNTS layers were investigated. According to XRD analysis, all layers are composed of CNTS phase and have been well crystallized in a cubic phase, with the crystallites oriented toward the (111) direction. The results of SEM analyses indicate that CNTS layers have a rather homogeneous and compact surface with very fine nodules. Thickness variation resulted a noticeably change in the optical band gap energy. Hall effect measurements show that all layers present a p-type conduction. From the I-V characteristics, we investigated that the CNTS/n-Si heterojunction exhibits a rectifying behavior. These results suggest that the CNTS layers are very suitable for low-cost photovoltaic applications.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Monocrystalline PV Panel Model with EIS Technique Based Internal Parameters Estimation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This work is aimed at estimating internal PV panel parameters under outdoor conditions by using the impedance spectroscopy technique. The impedance is measured by leaving the PV panel in the real operative status corresponding to three operation zones: the open voltage circuit zone, the maximum power point zone and the short current zone. Since variations on the shunt resistance are associated with multiple short-term defaults, this study seeks to estimate changes in this parameter using a dynamic model fitted to the experimental impedance measurements. The results show that the shunt resistance of the PV panel is strongly dependent on both irradiance and operation zone, which can be used to diagnose the PV panel and the DC side of the PV installation. Moreover, a two-diode dynamic model considering this dynamic resistance and the junction capacitance effect is deduced and validated through Matlab/Simulink interface. The obtained model provides higher accuracy in comparison with the shunt resistance variation identified through other analytic methods. Thus, this dynamic model is feasible for detecting several defects affecting the PV systems under outdoor conditions.

articleTitle: Modeling of GaN HEMT I-V Characteristics Using Artificial Intelligence: Optimization Study
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The drain-source current versus the drain-source voltage characteristics (Ids-Vds) of the Gallium Nitride (GaN) HEMT are modeled by applying the Artificial Neural Networks (ANN) approach. This modeling method needs a great amount of training data, which means that we had to measure many Ids-Vds characteristics for different gate source voltages (V gs) values that is not of well practice. Furthermore, an arbitrary choice of the samples used in the training process can increase the model error. An accurate method for optimizing the number and the values of V gs values, utilized in the training step, and for optimizing the ANN neurons number is carried out. We have used the Genetic Algorithm (GA) and the Levenberg-Marquard Algorithm (LMA) to optimize the ANN weights and biases. A weak model error is achieved with the LMA optimizer by applying the mean square error as a fitness function. Then an optimization algorithm is developed in the purpose to get optimal values and numbers of V gs and to get optimal numbers of ANN neurons for ANN training. The optimization methodology is validated by using simulated Ids-Vds curves.

articleTitle: Smart and Portable Neurotransmitters Sensors Based on Screen Printed Electrodes : The case of Serotonin and Dopamine Analysis
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Neurotransmitters play a vital role in numerous bodily systems, influencing functions such as cognition, mood, and metabolism. Dopamine (DA) and Serotonin (5-HT) are two key neurotransmitters with profound impacts on health and behavior. The dysregulation of their levels is associated with a number of diseases, which makes the simultaneous quantification of both essential for the understanding and treatment of such conditions. Electrochemical sensors have been utilized for the detection of both neurotransmitters due to their sensitivity, selectivity, and simplicity. The integration of screen-printed electrode (SPE) with electrochemical sensors presents an opportunity for the development of miniaturized and portable devices for rapid analysis. Moreover, modified SPE has been demonstrated to be capable of the concurrent detection of DA and 5-HT, despite the overlapping of their oxidation potentials. In this paper, we present an overview of the existing literature on the individual and simultaneous electrochemical detection of DA and 5-HT using screen-printed electrodes. This will provide insights into the advancements and challenges in this field.

articleTitle: ECG Monitor Design: From One to Three - Advancing ECG Monitoring with AI-Generated Lead Synthesis (GANs)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Accurate and continuous monitoring of heart rate and rhythm is crucial for the diagnosis and management of various cardiovascular diseases. Traditional 12-lead electrocardiograms (ECGs) provide comprehensive information about cardiac electrical activity but require multiple electrodes and wired connections, limiting their use in ambulatory settings. To address these limitations, we explored the possibility of synthesizing a complete 3-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) from a single available lead using a generative adversarial network (GAN). The GAN is designed to learn the anatomical and physiological relationships between different leads, capturing specific features of ECG signals. The generator architecture is adapted to account for anatomical differences, incorporating modules specific to each lead. Medical constraints are integrated into the training process to ensure physiological coherence in the generated signals. This innovative approach allows for detailed insights into cardiac electrical activity from a single measurement point, offering a practical and precise solution for advanced cardiac monitoring. The findings of this research open up new possibilities in the field of remote medical monitoring and cardiac disorder management.

articleTitle: Optimization of Network Voltage Losses and Deviation Electricity Including a Photovoltaic Plant
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The advancement of technology has led to an increase in energy consumption. Consequently, the growing demand for power generation and transportation has resulted in new constraints in terms of reducing gas emissions and the need to adopt renewable sources. This has led to the expansion of electrical networks, which have become increasingly large and complicated. The formulation of the problem must take into account a number of constraints, including those related to the voltage energy balance, the voltages of generator nodes, reactive productions at generator nodes, and the production capacity. A series of load flow studies were conducted using the standard Newton-Raphson method and the incorporation of an optimization method based on particle swarm optimization (PSO) for both the IEEE 30-bus standard system and the IEEE 30-bus system integrating a photovoltaic power plant. The simulations were performed using MATLAB. The objective was to identify optimal strings for the bus parameters that minimized transmission losses and the sum of voltage deviations of all consuming nodes.

articleTitle: Enhanced Diagnosis of Lithium-Ion Battery Health in Electric Vehicles Through Advanced Hybrid Deep Learning Model Incorporating Attention Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: With the rising adoption of lithium-ion batteries(LIBs) in electric vehicles, significant research efforts have been dedicated to ensuring the safe and reliable performance of Battery Management Systems (BMS). Accurately estimating the State of Health (SOH), a crucial aspect of BMS functionality, is imperative for the secure operation of electric vehicles. To tackle this challenge, we propose a time series model designed specifically for forecasting the State of Health (SOH) of Li-ion batteries. Our approach integrates a CNN with a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) architecture, augmented by an attention mechanism. Experimental findings demonstrate that this LSTM-based approach significantly enhances prediction accuracy. The outcomes of this investigation present a promising avenue for improving the dependability and efficiency of electric vehicle battery systems, ultimately advancing the widespread adoption and sustainability of electric transportation.

articleTitle: Structural and Optical Properties of Cu2NiSnS4 thin Films Synthesized Through Thermal Evaporation Technique
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper investigates the physical properties of the thermally evaporated earth-abundant Cu2NiSnS4 (CNTS) thin films grown on glass substrates that are either unheated or heated to 100 or 200°C. The as-grown films deposited on unheated substrates were then annealed in air at 100°C, 200, and 300°C. The samples' crystalline structure was examined using the X-ray diffraction technique. The obtained XRD patterns indicated amorphous structure for as grown and air annealed films. Whereas those deposited, respectively, on 100°C and 200°C heated substrates displayed the appearance of CNTS related peaks. The estimated crystallite size average was found to be roughly 19 nm. CNTS thin-film optical properties were analyzed using UV-VIS-NIR spectrophotometry. The optical measurements demonstrated that the films had significant visible range absorption coefficient (10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">5</sup>–10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>cm-1). The CNTS sample's direct band-gap was determined to be between 1.77 and 1.57 eV. Electrically, using the hot probe method, the electrical p-type conductivity of CNTS thin coating was confirmed. These characteristics make CNTS thin films appropriate as an active layer for solar cell applications.

articleTitle: New Molecularly Imprinted Polymer-MOF Sensor for Urea Optimized by an Artificial Neural Network (ANN)
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This study focuses on the development and optimization of a modified electrode for urea detection using a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP)@ZIF-7 composite. The electrode surface was prepared by mechanical polishing followed by electropolishing in H<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>SO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>, and then modified by electropolymerization of pyrrole in LiClO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> solution. Factors influencing the performance of the electrode were systematically investigated using Plackett-Burman Design (PBD) for screening and Central Composite Design (CCD) for optimization. An artificial neural network (ANN) model was trained to predict the electrochemical response based on various parameters. The ANN showed high prediction accuracy with <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> values of 0.96815 (training), 0.9917 (validation) and 0.9937 (test). The optimized electrode showed excellent performance in urea detection as evidenced by differential pulse voltammetry with a linear response range from <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{10}^{-\mathbf{11}}$</tex> to <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{10}^{-\mathbf{5}}\mathbf{M}$</tex> and a low detection limit of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{5.10}^{-\mathbf{12}}\ \mathbf{M}$</tex>. Overall, this study highlights the effectiveness of the MIP@ZIF-7 modified electrode for sensitive and selective urea detection.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Efficiency of Silicon Solar Cells: An Optimization Approach Using the Taguchi Method and Artificial Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This study aims to improve the efficiency of silicon solar cells by optimizing key parameters through a hybrid optimization approach. The goal is to achieve maximum performance while maintaining cost effectiveness in photovoltaic systems. We used a one-dimensional silicon p-n junction model simulated with COMSOL Multiphysics 6.2. The Taguchi method was used to analyze various process variables, and an artificial neural network (ANN) was trained with data from a full factorial design to predict the optimal configurations for the solar cells. The combined Taguchi-ANN approach successfully identified an optimal set of parameters that resulted in a significant increase in the efficiency of the silicon solar cells, achieving a peak efficiency of 25.41 %. The integration of Taguchi and ANN provides a comprehensive framework for optimizing silicon solar cells, offering significant efficiency improvements and paving the way for more advanced, cost-effective photovoltaic systems.

articleTitle: A Box-Behnken and TLBO-ANN Method for Optimizing Hydrogen Generation via NaBH4 Hydrolysis Using β-Ketoenamine Co (II) Catalysts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This study investigates the synthesis and application of a <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\beta$</tex> -ketoenamine cobalt (II) catalyst for hydrogen production via the hydrolysis of sodium borohydride (NaBH4). All reagents were of analytical grade and the catalyst was prepared using Schlenk techniques. The hydrogen generation rate (HGR) was measured under various conditions, including different concentrations of NaBH4 and NaOH, and different reaction temperatures. The experimental design used a Box-Behnken design (BBD) to evaluate the effects of five factors on the HGR. The results were modeled using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and a TLBO-ANN model to predict and optimize the HGR. The RSM model achieved an R2 value of 0.7859, indicating a good fit, but with significant prediction errors. In contrast, the TLBO-ANN model showed high prediction accuracy with an R2 value of 0.9997 and minimal bias. The study concludes that temperature and NaBH4 mass significantly affect HGR, and the TLBO-ANN model provides a robust tool for optimizing hydrogen production processes.

articleTitle: Plackett-Burman Design and Artificial Neural Network for Optimization of Electrothermal Response of GAAFET Transistor
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this study, Plackett-Burman design and artificial neural network (ANN) models are used to optimize the thermal and electrical responses of gate all-around field effect transistor (GAAFET) devices. The MLR models derived from the PBD design showed moderate performance in predicting electrical responses, with significant errors and moderate explanatory power. However, the thermal response model showed strong predictive ability with low errors. ANOVA analysis highlighted key factors influencing the electrical and thermal responses, such as gate voltage and drain voltage. Subsequently, ANN models were developed that exhibited superior predictive accuracy for electrical and thermal responses, with high <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{R}^{\mathbf{2}}$</tex> values during the training, validation, and test phases. The results suggest that while MLR models provide initial information, ANN models provide robust and accurate predictions, thereby improving the design and optimization of GAAFET transistors for high performance applications.

articleTitle: Optimized Inverse Kinematics of a 2-DoF Robotic Manipulator Using a Hybrid Approach Combining an ANN with a Metaheuristic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Resolving the Inverse Kinematics (IK) problem is critical for investigating 2-DoF robotic manipulators in complex environments. Traditional analytical methods often struggle with the inherent nonlinearity of these problems. This paper presents a hybrid approach combining Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) and Genetic Algorithm (GA) with ANNs to to obtain the hyperparameters for the architecture of ANNs such as the hidden layer size, and the activation function. The proposed methodology introduces a hyperparameter optimization technique for training the ANNs, using a Random step-size dataset, effectively leveraging the strengths of both metaheuristic algorithms and ANNs. Experimental results are conducted to show the efficiency of the proposed hybrid approach in the computation of the IK of the 2-DoF robotic manipulator, with the Mean Squared Error (MSE) values for PSO-ANN and GA-ANN being around 8.7954e-7 and 8.9492e-5, respectively.

articleTitle: Investigating Optimal Tracking Intervals for Solar Tracking Systems to Enhance Efficiency and Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Conventional solar trackers continuously adjust solar panels to optimize energy production, a process that can consume significant energy, potentially surpassing the energy gained. This research examines the most effective tracking interval for solar tracking systems to mitigate this issue. Through testing with intervals ranging from 5 minutes to 5 hours, it was determined that setting tracking intervals no shorter than 1 hour and no longer than 2 hours and 30 minutes is recommended to achieve a balance between energy efficiency and production. Additionally, this study suggests that elevation and azimuth angles should not be tracked using the same time periods; instead, a 2-hour interval for elevation tracking and a 3-hour interval for azimuth angle tracking are advised for optimal performance. The proposed discrete tracking method consumes less than 0.15% of the energy produced, thereby enhancing energy efficiency, reducing unnecessary energy consumption, and improving the overall reliability and lifespan of solar tracking systems. This approach has the potential to significantly impact the future of solar power by enhancing the efficiency and reliability of solar tracking systems, thereby increasing the viability and appeal of solar energy as a primary renewable resource.

articleTitle: Smart Device for Monitoring Persons with Alzheimer Disease
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease, affecting millions globally, presents significant health challenges that require specialized attention. Continuous medical follow-up is crucial for early diagnosis, effective symptom management, and providing necessary support to patients and their families. In the biomedical field, innovative systems like the “Kiwatch” video surveillance camera and the “ELLiQ” robot have been developed to monitor individuals with Alzheimer's. However, these solutions have notable limitations, particularly in real-time tracking of patient location and physiological parameters. Currently, no device on the market combines both functions. To address these gaps, this paper proposes a smart device for the remote monitoring of Alzheimer's patients, focusing on key metrics such as location tracking, body temperature, and heart rate. We developed a smart portable system, a functional prototype integrating an Arduino Mega board, a temperature sensor, a heartbeat sensor, and a Bluetooth module. This setup enables the transmission of vital health information to a smartphone via the Bluetooth Terminal application. Rigorous testing was conducted to evaluate the prototype's effectiveness in the remote monitoring of Alzheimer's patients

articleTitle: Impact of Pollution on PV Module and Proposed Solutions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The work presented in this paper aims to study the impact of pollution on the production of photovoltaic systems. The work proposes the establishment of a supervision and control system allowing real-time knowledge of the different sizes of the PV system as well as automatic intervention in the event of accumulation of dust or other. The communication with the operator is ensured by the GSM network. The proposed work is presented as a simple and easy solution that can be used to ensure good control of photovoltaic systems in polluted areas.

articleTitle: Transition to Electric Vehicle Charging Station Market-A Review in Russian Context
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: During the COVID-19 pandemic and 2022 crises, Russia experienced a 34% increase in electric car sales, while overall passenger and light commercial vehicle sales dropped by 60% or more. Russia's concept for the development of electric vehicles predicts one in ten cars will be electric by 2030, with 220,000 electric cars planned to be manufactured annually within eight years, exceeding 1.4 million. This study analyzes the current market situation and prioritizes solutions for the market of Russian electric vehicle charging infrastructure.

articleTitle: Experimental Performance Comparison of a One-Axis Sun Tracking Versus Fixed Silicon PV Module
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive experimental study comparing the performance of a one-axis sun tracking system with a fixed silicon photovoltaic (PV) module setup. The investigation evaluates the energy generation and efficiency of both configurations under real-world conditions. The results provide valuable insights into the effectiveness of sun tracking technology in enhancing solar energy harvesting.

articleTitle: A Model-Based Parametric of a Large-Scale Hybrid Microgrid with Battery Storage Supplying a Residential Load
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this paper, a dynamic simulator of a solar-wind microgrid with batteries is developed to meet the energy needs of a habitat. The paper attempts to formulate accurate models for the system components, show the ways for performance testing, and account for the techno-economic considerations. Two indicators are developed based on parametric sensitivity algorithm: 1) loss of power supply probability as technical indicator and 2) levelized cost of energy as economic indicator. An energy management system has been developed to share power between the load and the battery. Data collection, energy resource evaluation, load profile study, and sensitivity testing are performed via a dynamic simulator. The results of the sensitivity analysis are necessary to determine the ranges of the decision variables of the hybrid microgrid to use them in the optimization process.

articleTitle: Robust Optimized Trading Strategies for Energy Commodity Markets
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The growth of renewable energy sources in the grid and the more recent outbreak of the Russian war on Ukraine have led to deep changes in the energy markets' dynamics. The prices have become more unstable and unpredictable, determining an overall higher liquidity and volatility. This caused a rising interest in the development of algorithmic trading strategies to support energy traders in their decisions. In this scenario, Evolutionary Algorithms represent a potent and effective tool to develop robust and innovative trading strategies. Indeed, their flexibility makes them suitable to include various performance metrics. In this article, the optimal closing criteria in an energy future market have been determined by means of a recently developed Evolutionary Algorithm, called Social Network Optimization. The trading strategy implemented, by exploiting five different self-defined parameters, shows profitable results over the nearly six years of data taken into consideration. In particular, it determines an overall average positive return and a maximum monthly yield equal to 1.9 %.

articleTitle: Selective Harmonic Mitigation of Cascaded H-Bridge Multilevel Converters Using Real-Coded Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this paper, the Real-Coded Genetic Algorithm (RCGA) is used to find appropriate switching angles for Selective Harmonic Mitigation (SHM) of Cascaded H-Bridge (CHB) multilevel inverters capable to meet the grid code standards for individual harmonics and total harmonic distortion (THD). The algorithm is tested on staircase multilevel waveforms. Simulation results show that the algorithm is able to find switching angles that meet the grid standards.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Tunisian Coin Recognition Embedded System with Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Managing a large volume of coins poses a complex challenge in various fields, particularly within Tunisian administrations, specifically in terms of counting and classification. In this case, several coin recognition systems are distinguished, such as systems based on mechanical, electromagnetic, and image processing methods. However, these systems may suffer from accuracy and reliability shortcomings and are sensitive to deception. To avoid these problems, we have developed an intelligent system based on convolutional models (CNN) with the aim of automating coin detection, classification, and counting. Additionally, we have expanded our database by integrating a generative neural network model (GAN). The main goal of our paper is to develop a robust and precise solution capable of efficiently processing a large volume of coins quickly and presenting the results in a mobile application connected to the system. Our work combines the latest technologies to assist Tunisian administrations in better managing their finances. The accuracy result has achieved up to 97.8 % with real time detection.

articleTitle: Innovative UV Water Treatment Solutions for Greenhouse Irrigation Using Intelligent MPPT
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: UV water treatment is essential for modern agriculture, particularly for greenhouse irrigation, as it ensures effective disinfection without the use of chemicals, thereby guaranteeing crop safety and sustainable use of water resources. In this study, we present the development and implementation of an intelligent Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) control system to optimize the operational parameters of a UV water treatment reactor, specifically the UV lamp intensity and the water flow rate, to ensure optimal water quality for greenhouse irrigation. The results demonstrate that the intelligent MPPT control effectively regulates these parameters, ensuring stable and reliable water treatment. By optimizing the exposure of contaminants to UV rays, the system maximizes pathogen inactivation and improves water safety. Furthermore, it was found that precise adjustments of UV intensity and water flow rate reduced variations in UV dose and improved treatment uniformity, leading to enhanced overall system performance.

articleTitle: Power Management in an Islanded Microgrid Using Droop Control of a Three-Level NPC Inverter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Multilevel inverter structures are widely used in microgrid due to the high power they support. These converters play the role of interface between the energy source; whether conventional or renewable; and the grid. In this paper, we present the application of single-phase three-level NPC inverter in an autonomous microgrid. This topology is widely used in different industrial applications. The Droop control is used in this work in order to share the power equally between the parallel inverters of the microgrid. This control also avoids the problem of circulation currents that can deteriorate power converters. The performance of the proposed configuration is presented in the simulation results.

articleTitle: State of Charge Estimation of Lithium-Ion Batteries Using Convolutional Neural Networks in Electric Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The emergence of Electric Vehicles (EVs) has introduced new issues and complexities, particularly in accurately gauging the remaining battery capacity or the distance an EV can travel before needing a recharge, known as the State of Charge (SoC) estimation problem. This study aims to develop an innovative solution to this problem while considering the usual computational complexity requirements. It emphasizes maintaining low memory and computational demands for practical implementation within a Battery Management System (BMS). By leveraging contemporary tools from artificial intelligence, especially Machine Learning (ML) models, the findings indicate that accurate SoC prediction can be achieved with simple ML models, given a well-curated dataset. Specifically, a Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) with two hidden layers and a limited number of hidden neurons shows promising results in estimating the SoC for a lithium-ion battery cell while maintaining low computational complexity. At 25°C, the CNN model reports a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.97 and a root mean squared error (RMSE) of 1.71. This research offers significant potential for future advancements in SoC estimation, providing a solid foundation for addressing the issue and suggesting an optimal ML architecture for future BMSs to improve the SoC prediction accuracy.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Transform Coding Module in the Post-VVC Standard
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The Enhanced Compression Model (ECM) serves as the software foundation for future video coding exploration, extending beyond the capabilities of the current Versatile Video Coding (VVC) standard. This paper conducts statistical analyses on ECM encoded videos, focusing particularly on 1D and 2D transformation types, as well as intra and inter prediction modes across videos from different classes with distinct resolutions. These analyses are performed at the decoder level, where the coding decisions have already been made by the encoder. Results reveal that the selection of transformation type and size, as well as prediction mode (intra or inter), depend on video characteristics such as motion and texture. This study represents a significant advancement in the development of intelligent algorithms based on video characteristics to expedite decision-making in the ECM encoding process.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study of MCSA and ZSV-Based Methods for Diagnosing Inter-Turn Short-Circuit Faults in Induction Motors
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Stator winding problems are widely known as the most common cause of induction motor breakdowns. In fact, these defects account for 20% to 40% of all problems in induction motor. One of the primary reasons for stator issues is inter-turn short-circuit faults, which can have severe and hazardous effects on both the motor and the connected electrical equipment. Therefore, early detection of inter-turn short-circuit faults can prevent breakdowns and enhance the reliability and safety of industrial facilities. In this context, this paper conducts a comparative study of two methods used to diagnose the ITSC fault in induction motors. The first method relies on motor current signature analysis (MCSA), whereas the second method focuses on monitoring the Zero-Sequence Voltage (ZSV). Several tests were performed on a three-phase 1.1-kW induction motor under both normal and faulty conditions. The obtained results illustrate the advantages of the ZSV analysis over the MCSA method in terms of reliability, rapidity and precision for diagnosing the occurrence of ITSC faults.

articleTitle: Improving NAO Robot Grasps with Deep Learning-Based Rectangle Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Robotic grasping precision is crucial for effective manipulation of objects in various applications, especially in manufacturing and robotics. This paper presents a novel approach to improve grasping performance for NAO robots. We propose a deep learning-based method that utilizes rectangle detection to enhance the accuracy and reliability of grasping tasks. The approach leverages Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) to identify optimal grasping rectangles within images of pieces. This enables the NAO robot to precisely grasp pieces based on their rectangular features, leading to a significant improvement in grasping success rates compared to traditional methods. The paper details the design of the CNN architecture, the training process, and the evaluation of the proposed method on real-world grasping tasks with the NAO robot. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach in achieving reliable and precise grasping, paving the way for more robust manipulation capabilities for NAO robots.

articleTitle: Sign Language Detection Based on Artificial Intelligence from Images
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper explores the intersection of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and sign language communication, aiming to enhance accessibility and inclusion for individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing. Sign language, with its rich system of gestures, facial expressions, and body movements, represents a unique form of deaf human communication. Leveraging the power of AI, particularly the UNET architecture, this study proposes a sign language detection system capable of analyzing images to translate sign language gestures into text or speech. The project encompasses stages from data collection to model training and performance evaluation. As a result, our model achieved a validation accuracy 95,51%. The findings offer promising prospects for advancing sign language recognition and translation through AI technologies.

articleTitle: Electrical Properties of Ag/Cu2CoSnS4/SnO2/FTO Thin Film Heterojunction
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Quaternary chalcogenide Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CoSnS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> (CCTS) thin films were successfully prepared by spray pyrolysis on FTO substrates pre-coated withSnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>, forming Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CoSnS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>/SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/FTO heterojunctions. Structural, morphological, and chemical properties of the Cu<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>CoSnS<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>/SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/FTO heterojunction were characterized using X-ray diffraction (XRD), scanning electron microscopy (SEM), and energy dispersive X-ray spectrometry (EDX). The I-V characteristics of the heterojunction under dark conditions exhibited rectification behavior. Additionally, the illuminated J-V analysis demonstrated a power conversion efficiency of 0.56% for the fabricated CCTS/SnO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>/FTO cell.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Half-Cut PV Market Modules in Outdoor Conditions
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Photo Voltaic (PV) technology continues to advance, seeking to optimize efficiency and performance. Half-cut and back contact PV modules have emerged as a promising innovation, aiming to enhance energy yield and durability. This study presents a comprehensive analysis of outdoor performance in normal operation considering four technologies of PV modules. The research focuses on evaluating the efficiency of these modules in real-world conditions. A dedicated outdoor test facility at SolarTechLAB exposed the modules to varying solar radiance and environmental factors. We measured the current-voltage (I-V) curves of each module, and we calculated the performance ratio using the lEC 61724–1 Standard. We determined that half- cut cells present a higher performance ratio than full-cell modules in a range between 3.7 to 7 %.

articleTitle: A Ringing Effect Mitigation Approach with Snubber Capacitors in a Dual Active Bridge Converter
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This work develops a design methodology for the snubber circuit of a dual-active bridge (DAB) converter affected by the ringing effect. In particular, the ringing is generated by the input and output planar transformer stray capacitances that interact with its leakage inductors. An asymmetric snubber circuit was designed to mitigate the ringing effect produced in the DAB prototype under investigation. The simulation studies show the effectiveness of the snubber circuit in mitigating the current amplitude during the ringing, preserving the DAB components from the current overshoots and extending their reliability.

articleTitle: Methodology of Construction of a Digital Twin: Application to the Stäubli Robot's Arm and Shoulder
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this paper, we present the development and analysis of a digital twin for the Stäubli robot's arm and shoulder. Using SIMULINK/MATLAB, we simulate the robot's normal operational behavior, focusing on its kinematics, dynamics, and control algorithms. This digital twin serves as a baseline for understanding the robot's standard functioning, facilitating performance optimization and predictive maintenance. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of digital twins in enhancing the reliability and efficiency of robotic systems.

articleTitle: Combined Mobilenet for Plant Diseases Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Plant disease is a major threat to global food security, as it can reduce crop yields and even lead to complete crop failure. The consequences can be devastating, causing food shortages, price increases, and potentially leading to famine and starvation. Various factors can cause plant diseases, such as fungi, viruses, and bacteria. Each disease has specific symptoms that can be identified by experts, which is crucial for accurate diagnosis and effective disease management. In this work, we propose a new lightweight architecture for classifying plant disease images. This architecture utilizes a pretrained MobilenetV3Large model and a modified version of the fused MBC block to improve the accuracy of plant disease detection. We employ transfer learning and a specialized training methodology to achieve faster convergence and higher accuracy. To evaluate and test our model, we use a dataset containing 7,586 images of pepper, potato, and strawberry diseases. Our results demonstrate that our model outperforms state-of-the-art architectures, achieving a remarkable 99.93% accuracy during the test phase.

articleTitle: Behavior Comparison of Hybrid Energy Storage Systems for Pulsed Loads in Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Pulsed loads are widely diffused on board of the electric vehicles and are related to different devices adopted or to the propulsion/traction performance of the vehicles (e.g. the power required in a vertical take-off by an UAV). This impulsive behavior plays a crucial role for the correct management and sizing of energy storage systems: usually, the combination of different type of storage systems are adopted with the aim to improve the performance of the system, reducing the weight and the occupied volume. The paper proposes the analysis of different configuration of hybrid storage system, based on lithium-ion batteries and supercapacitors, able to supply a power pulsed load: the aim is the investigation of the different behavior of the configurations considering also the dynamic influence of the control in the power supply of the pulsed load. The results are obtained using numerical simulations.

articleTitle: Physical Properties of Cu12Sb4S13 Thin Films Deposited at Oblique Incidence by Vacuum Thermal Evaporation
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The aim of this work is to elaborate and characterize thin films of the Cu12Sb4S13 material which are prepared by vacuum thermal evaporation onto unheated glass substrates at obliquely incident angles (00-85°). We have shown by X-ray diffraction of the Cu12Sb4S13 powder that only the cubic phase is present with the orientation along the (222) plane. The reflection and transmission spectra show the presence of interference fringes which prove the homogeneity of the prepared thin films. The thicknesses of the thin films decrease by increasing the incident angle from 533 to 102 nm. A high absorption coefficient of more than 105 cm-1 was established. The allowed direct transitions increase by increasing the incident angle ranging from 1.42 to 2.49 eV. The electrical measurements show that our thin layer keeps the type of conductivity that is p for the different angles. The resistivity and the concentration of the free charge carriers evolve proportionally with the angles of inclination, while the mobility evolves proportionally opposite which confirms the amorphous appearance.

articleTitle: Performances Comparison of Passive Filters in SiC-Based Three Phase Grid Connected Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper presents the design of an LCL filter for grid -connected three-phase converters. In particular, an analysis was conducted on an LCL filter for a converter with a rated power of 10 kVA, considering the implementation of a space vector modulation at a frequency of 20 kHz. The passive filter has been designed with particular attention paid to the performance of the individual components. A detailed analysis of the passive filter impedance has enabled the definition of the effective behaviour of the implemented filter for the specific modulation frequency. The experimental results for the LCL filter and corresponding Land LC topologies concerning a SiC- based three-phase converter have been presented and compared in order to evaluate their performance and validate the filter design process.

articleTitle: A Flexible Transmission Scheme of Instantaneous Pulsating Power for Large-Capacity CHB-QAB Based Offshore Wind Power Converters
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In a modified cascaded H-bridge (CHB) converter for large, e.g., 10MW+ offshore wind turbines, the instantaneous pulsating power (DC power + 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-order-frequency pulsating power) flows into the quad-active-bridge (QAB) converter and causes 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-order-frequency oscillations of the input currents. These oscillations increase the current stress on the switching devices and the power losses in the QAB converter. Therefore, this paper proposes a flexible transmission scheme for instantaneous power to optimize the performance of the modified CHB-QAB converter. Specifically, the DC power remains to be transmitted to the grid-side converter, while the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-order-frequency pulsating power is flexibly transmitted to the DC-bus capacitors and the QAB converter to reduce 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-order-frequency oscillations. To control the DC power and the 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-order-frequency pulsating power separately, a summation differential (SD) decoupled control strategy is also proposed to decouple the above coupled instantaneous power. With the proposed flexible transmission scheme, 2<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">nd</sup>-order-frequency oscillations can be greatly optimized, and the power losses and the current stress in the QAB converter can all be decreased. These improvements contribute to the operation of the QAB converter. A 20MW simulation is presented to validate the feasibility of the proposed flexible transmission scheme.

articleTitle: Technical, Economical, and Environmental Optimization Analysis of the Hybrid Energy System on Djerba Island
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The objective of the research consists in providing a technical-economic, and environmental assessment of renewable energy resource options. A hybrid system consisting of photovoltaic, wind turbine, tidal turbine, and hydraulic power with battery was developed from outside the network, with diesel generators providing backup power. The design of the system has been analyzed with Hybrid Multi-Energy Resource Optimization software, which simulates and optimizes the distribution of energy based on consumption and energy sources, as well as calculating pollutant gas emissions. The financial report calculated the net present and total energy unit costs. This system has been designed to satisfy the demand for energy in south-eastern Tunisia on the island of Djerba. The suggested system is the best because it considers power generation, cost of energy, emissions, and net present cost.

articleTitle: A New Neural Network Architecture for Single Agent Control in Urban Traffic Network
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: Traffic congestion in urban areas presents difficulties, such as increased waiting times and dissatisfaction among commuters. Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL) offers remedies by allowing agents to acquire optimal strategies. This study delves into the application of DRL in enhancing urban traffic signal systems. Recent progress in reinforcement learning, which includes the utilization of deep neural networks and the integration of real-time data, holds the potential for intelligent adaptive traffic signals. This article introduces a novel intelligent sequential methodology known as SSE_DQN (Self Sequential Estimator Deep Q Network), which improves learning efficiency by integrating concepts such as optimal lane changes and responsive reactions to dynamic conditions. SSE_DQN stands as a significant breakthrough that could potentially mitigate congestion and enhance the efficiency of urban transportation. Through both simulations and real-world experimentation, its ability to adapt to traffic patterns is effectively demonstrated. This study contributes to the development of intelligent transportation systems, highlighting the potential of DRL in addressing urban challenges.

articleTitle: Advanced Pattern Detection and Trend Forecasting in European Carbon Markets Using Machine Learning Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This paper investigates the detection and prediction of patterns in European Carbon Emission price trends using machine learning on high-frequency tick-by-tick data, resampled at 5-minute intervals. After data preprocessing to manage outliers and ensure data integrity, trends in close prices were identified through pivot points and percentage change thresholds. Five machine learning models, including, Linear Regression, Decision Tree Regressor, K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) Regressor, Random Forest Regressor, and Gradient Boosting Regressor were trained and evaluated for pattern prediction and classification tasks. The Gradient Boosting Regressor emerged as the top performer, achieving the lowest test Mean Squared Error (MSE) and the highest R2 score, outperforming KNN and Decision Tree models by approximately 20% in MSE. It also achieved the highest F1 Score in pattern classification, underscoring its superior accuracy and reliability in analyzing complex financial data. This study offers valuable insights for future financial data analysis, presenting robust methods for predicting and classifying price trends.

articleTitle: A Dynamic Equalization Topology Based on Auxiliary Cell: Theoretical and Simulative Analyses
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: The dynamic equalization approach can significantly increase the use of electric vehicle second-life batteries in stationary applications. Dynamic equalization aims to face the very high variability of the capacity values of the second-life battery cells that strongly reduces the battery usable capacity. This work proposes an alternative dynamic equalization architecture based on an auxiliary cell to support the less-performing cells, maximizing the battery usable capacity. A theoretical methodology has been presented to analyze the proposed architecture. The obtained preliminary theoretical results are then validated using a simulation platform. The final results show a potential increase in usable battery energy of up to 16 % using an ideal DC/DC converter, and 13 % with a DC/DC converter efficiency of 0.8.

articleTitle: Response Surface Methodology and Support Vector Regression for the Optimization of Hydrogen Generation via NaBH4 Hydrolysis Using $\beta$ - Ketoenamine Nickel Catalysts
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This study investigates the hydrogen generation rate (HGR) from the hydrolysis of sodium borohydride (NaBH4) using response surface methodology (RSM) and support vector regression (SVR) models. Analytical grade reagents were used under controlled conditions and catalysts were prepared using standard Schlenk techniques. The Box-Behnken design (BBD) was used to evaluate the effects of various factors on HGR. The RSM model obtained a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 1800.37, a Variance Accounted For (V AF) of 72.68%, a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of 104.38%, and an R2 of 0.726807. In contrast, the SVR model showed superior performance with an RMSE of 67.487943, a V AF of 99.96%, a MAPE of 0.444621, and an R2, Adj-R2, and Pred-R2 of 0.999616. The SVR model demonstrated the highest accuracy and robustness, closely matching the observed data and effectively capturing the underlying relationships, making it a more reliable tool for predicting HGR in this study.

articleTitle: Optimizing Hydrogen Production from NaBH4 Hydrolysis Using BBD, ANN, and Genetic Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: This study investigates the optimization of hydrogen generation rate (HGR) by NaBH4 hydrolysis using a comprehensive approach integrating experimental design, response surface methodology (RSM), artificial neural networks (ANN), and genetic algorithms (GA). Catalyst synthesis and Box-Behnken design were used to investigate the effects of temperature, stirring rate, NaBH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> and catalyst masses, and NaOH concentration on HGR. The RSM-built quadratic regression model highlighted significant effects of temperature, NaBH4 mass, and catalyst mass on HGR. ANN modeling demonstrated strong predictive performance, explaining 98% of the variance with a mean absolute percentage error (MAPE) of 0.065, root mean square error (RMSE) of 304.06, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> of 0.98. GA optimization indicated that the maximum HGR of 6912 mL/min.gcata can be achieved at 55°C, 150 mg NaBH4, 10 mg catalyst, and 0.7 mol/L NaOH concentration. In addition, the activation energy for NaBH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf> hydrolysis was determined to be 49.72 kJ/mol, which is in agreement with literature values.

articleTitle: A Comprehensive Design With Comparative Analysis of ANN-Based STSMC and Optimized PI Compensator for DC-DC Converter Feeding CPLs
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: In this article, a neural network based on the Super-Twisting sliding mode control (STSMC) is proposed for controlling the voltage of a DC-DC converter in an embedded propulsion system under constant power load (CPL). The converter model is then linearized in the neighborhood of the equilibrium point method, and optimal parameters for the PI compensator in various local operating regions are determined. Data collected through the STSMC approach are used as features and targets for training an Artificial Neural Network (ANN). An adjustable STSMC with tuned parameters supplied by ANN is tested by numerical simulations on a DC-DC converter, specifically a boost converter. The results demonstrate that the ANN-based approach offers superior dynamic voltage response compared to both the STSMC controller and conventional PI controller, with shorter stabilization times and minimal overshoot.

articleTitle: Numerical Simulation of Absorber and Buffer Layers Properties Effect on CZTS Based Solar Cell Using SCAPS-1D
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
abstract: SCAPS-1D was used in this paper to investigate the impact of thickness and gap energy of the CZTS absorber and buffer layer Zn (O, S) on the performance of the solar cell. We begin with introducing the experimental thickness and band gap of 608nm and 1.50 eV respectively, and we have found: an open circuit voltage <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{V}_{\mathbf{oc}}=\mathbf{1.16}\ \mathbf{V}$</tex> and the conversion efficiency of solar light to electricity was more than 15%. At the second point, we have varied the thickness and gap and we observed that the simulated cell had best thickness and gap energy of 2500 nm and 1.47 eV. These new values have led to our optimum device revealed these results an efficiency above 21%.

articleTitle: Performance Evaluation of Neural Network Models for Fuel Cell Power Prediction in Hybrid Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2024 IEEE International Conference on Artificial Intelligence & Green Energy (ICAIGE)
